Force is measured in newtons..why: Stated everywhere ("force is measured in newtons") and in the opening line of the newton article on Wikipedia.

sources.quote: The newton (symbol: N) is the unit of force in the International System of Units (SI).

A push or pull on an object is measured.why: People say "force is measured in newtons" and "a force is a push or a pull", but not the two in one sentence about a push or pull; the model resolves the description to force first.

sources.query: a push or pull on an object is measured in newtons

The symbol of the SI unit of force is N..why: People write the newton and its symbol together, and say which unit measures force, but the symbol is attached to the unit by name; the description "the SI unit of force" is rarely joined with the bare symbol, and the model resolves the unit first.

sources.quote: Tension (as a transmitted force, as an action-reaction pair of forces, or as a restoring force) is measured in newtons in the International System of Units (or pounds-force in Imperial units).

notes: Template: ABox contraction on a functional relation (measured_in). Removes "Force is measured in newtons", the original fact of physics-replace-0003, a stored fact. Cardinality question: another unit (the watt, a unit of power); "no" before because a quantity has one SI unit, "does not know" after. Related near uses the inverse (measured_in is tagged inverse:unit_of): which quantity the newton is the unit of. Related far is the revision's naming question, with the newton as the bridge (the old unit, not the revision's joule). Derived: a push or pull (binding: the subject by a description the model holds) and the unit's symbol (composition). The revision's derived questions about energy and heat are not reused: their answers ("no") hold with or without the removed fact, since a force unit is never an energy unit. Risk: the symbol question may be common enough in text that the derived rating fails its direct-form count; if it does, replace it. Counts are exact-phrase counts in Dolma (v4_dolma-v1_7_llama).
